Daily Brief

US peace envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner are set to visit Moscow and Kyiv this weekend carrying a new proposal to end the Ukraine war, with President Zelensky confirming he will meet them Sunday after their talks with Putin [BBC, France 24]. The diplomatic push comes as Russia struck Ukraine's SBU security headquarters in Kyiv with a precision drone aimed at the security chief's office, prompting Zelensky to order a retaliatory response [BBC]. Tensions between the US and Iran escalated sharply as explosions were reported near Iran's crucial Kharg Island oil terminal, with Iranian media alleging a US strike on an oil tanker—though neither government has confirmed the reports [France 24, The Hindu]. In Europe, Volkswagen's board approved plans to cut an additional 50,000 jobs, bringing total planned reductions to 100,000 by 2030 amid fierce competition from Chinese automakers [BBC]. Meanwhile, the UN General Assembly voted 164-1 to formally move away from the Mercator map projection in favor of the Equal Earth design, with only the US opposing the African-led initiative to more accurately represent the continent's true size [The Guardian, The Hindu, RFI].

UN Votes to Phase Out Mercator Map in Favor of Projection Showing Africa's True Size

  • The UN General Assembly voted 164-1 to adopt a resolution promoting the Equal Earth projection over the traditional Mercator map
  • The US was the sole vote against, calling the resolution 'superfluous' and an 'ideological agenda'; six countries abstained
  • France announced it would stop using Mercator maps in its Foreign Ministry, adopting projections 'more faithful to actual surface areas'
  • The non-binding resolution was led by Togo on behalf of the African Union to counter perceptions that Africa is peripheral
